topic: Working with files in the repo
objective: A trainee should be able to handle the expert's file-related workflow in their repo unsupervised, though the exact task is still unclear.

coverage.name: Purpose and context
coverage.description: What the file task is, why it matters, and which repo and project it belongs to.

coverage.name: Repo layout and file locations
coverage.description: Where the relevant files live, folder structure, naming conventions, and how to get access to the repo.

coverage.name: Tools and setup
coverage.description: Git tooling, editors, branches, permissions, and local configuration needed before starting.

coverage.name: Steps of the workflow
coverage.description: The actual sequence from start to finish: creating, editing, committing, reviewing, merging or deploying.

coverage.name: Judgement calls
coverage.description: How to decide what to change, where a file belongs, when to branch, and when it is ready to commit or merge.

coverage.name: Quirks and local problems
coverage.description: Odd behaviours, stale or untrustworthy files, merge conflicts, large files, ignored files, and the workarounds used.

coverage.name: Risks and consequences
coverage.description: What breaks if a file is wrongly changed, deleted, or committed, such as secrets, overwritten work, or broken builds, and how to recover.

coverage.name: People and unwritten rules
coverage.description: Who reviews, who approves, who owns which files, and team conventions for commits and pull requests.

coverage.name: Personal tips and checks
coverage.description: Habits the expert uses to work faster and safer, and checks done automatically before finishing.
